CriterionIn.description: One acceptance criterion: one rule the feature has to obey.

id.description: Your id for this criterion. Use the shape "AC-1" and it is kept exactly. Leave it out and ids are given in order: AC-1, AC-2, AC-3. Any other shape is renumbered to AC-1…AC-n by position — the answer says so in notes, and the ids in your test cases' "covers" are renumbered to match.
id.title: Id

text.description: The rule in one sentence, with the real numbers in it. "The account locks for 30 minutes after 5 wrong passwords" — not "the account locks quickly".
text.title: Text

CriterionIn.title: CriterionIn

MatrixIn.description: How much of a test matrix the planned runs actually cover.

covered_pairs.description: How many of those pairs the runs reach.
covered_pairs.title: Covered Pairs

factors.description: What varies between runs, such as ["browser", "device"].
factors.title: Factors

manual_only.description: How many runs nobody can automate.
manual_only.title: Manual Only

valid_pairs.description: How many pairs of values are worth covering.
valid_pairs.title: Valid Pairs

MatrixIn.title: MatrixIn

RiskIn.description: One way the feature could fail, scored the way an FMEA scores it.

category.description: One of: security, performance, reliability, data, usability, accessibility, functional. Anything else is read as functional.
category.title: Category

covered_by.description: The test ids you believe already reach this risk. The check reads the tests themselves and will disagree if the words do not.
covered_by.title: Covered By

detectability.description: How hard it is to notice, 1 to 5. 5 means nobody would.
detectability.title: Detectability

effect.description: What the user suffers when it happens.
effect.title: Effect

id.description: Your id for this risk, such as "R1".
id.title: Id

related_criteria.description: The criterion ids this risk belongs to, such as ["AC-2"].
related_criteria.title: Related Criteria

test_idea.description: One line saying what a test for this would do.
test_idea.title: Test Idea

RiskIn.title: RiskIn

covers.description: The criterion ids this test proves, such as ["AC-1", "AC-3"]. Use the same ids you sent in criteria. A criterion no test names is reported as having no tests.
covers.title: Covers

expected.description: What must be true afterwards, worded so it can only be true or false. "The page shows: Locked for 30 minutes" — not "it works".
expected.title: Expected

id.description: Your id for this test, such as "TC-04".
id.title: Id

kind.description: What kind of test this is. "normal" is the path that works; "wrong input" is bad data or no permission; "at the limit" uses the exact boundary value; "unusual" is everything rarer.
kind.title: Kind

steps.description: What the tester does, one action per step. At least one.
steps.title: Steps

test_data.description: The exact values this test uses: the amount, the file size, the number of tries. Say "$50.00", not "an order over the limit".
test_data.title: Test Data

title.description: What this test proves, in one line.
title.title: Title

description: Everything the release decision is made from.

accepted.description: Risk ids the team has accepted in writing. An accepted risk is still shown, with its id, but it no longer counts as untested.
accepted.title: Accepted

context.description: Anything else that decides the answer: limits, rules.
context.title: Context

matrix_summary.description: The test matrix, if you planned one. Leave it out and the matrix check comes back "not done yet".

risks.description: The risks, if you scored any. Leave it out and the risk check comes back "not done yet" — never "fine".
risks.title: Risks

story.description: The user story or the bug, in the words the team wrote.
story.title: Story

test_cases.description: The tests written for those criteria.
test_cases.title: Test Cases

title: ShipIn
